decisions.rationale: Verified: section.pep-recap (line 645) is outside every [data-pep-activity] and render() only hides activity sections (line 745), so the recap and cheat sheet show under Activity 1 from first load. The cheat sheet gives Activity 1's keyed listener (event.target.closest("button.like"); if (!btn) return; item.textContent = untrusted), Activity 2's full ordering rule, and Activity 3's keyed branch (problem+json -> problem.detail, otherwise a server message); the recap's 'show detail for what to fix' separates C from D. Workflow 2.3: judge whether 'any answer is semantically disclosed despite scanner passes'. Required fix: before an activity settles, no visible recap or cheat-sheet text may state that activity's discriminating answer; either reveal both only once the page is complete (still printed and present without JavaScript, gates still passing) or make them generic so they do not reproduce option code.

Verified line 470 sits in [data-pep-teaching] before the options and states the whole answer rule: the body runs to the first await, the rest waits as a microtask 'even if the promise was already fulfilled' (distractor C's trap), and 'Plain code finishes first, then every microtask, then the next task' (distractors D and A). Line 458's 'Commit to an order before you read the reminders under it' cannot be enforced and conflicts with the contract rules 'The learner predicts before any teaching' and that all instructions precede the interaction. module.json declares only 'an async body runs until its first await' as a joining detail. Required fix: remove the reminders and the 'commit before you read' sentence from the pre-check region; keep at most the declared joining detail in one sentence if needed, and move the queue rule into a hint step or post-check feedback.

Verified line 397 (data-pep-fit-good): 'build items with DOM methods, insert data as text, and let one parent listener handle every item' precedes the task and is the keyed construction, ruling out option C. Contract: the fit section 'contains no activity answer.' Required fix: keep the authentic untrusted-versus-own-markup decision and boundary, but state the good fit as the situation (content from visitors or an API, including items added later) without the implementation recipe.

Verified Activity 3 hint 2 (line 589): '... which problem details member explains this particular occurrence rather than naming the kind of error' is the definition of detail versus title and decides C versus D. Activity 1 hint 2 (line 418): 'Rule out any option that still hands visitor text to an API that parses HTML' eliminates C outright. Contract, Progressive optional hints: a hint 'does not give the answer'. Required fix: both final hints must pose the next reasoning step as something the learner does (e.g. tracing the scenario's body or the text's path) without stating the rule that eliminates a specific option.

Verified line 620: option D reads 'The same branch as the problem details option, but with showMessage(problem.title).' It labels C as 'the problem details option', cueing C/D as the finalists, and it is not self-contained in the static alternative or to a screen reader, unlike the other three code options. Required fix: make D a self-contained option parallel in form to A-C (full code, or a different self-contained misconception) with no reference to another option.

Verified: the listener bug 'if (event.target.matches("li"))' is events-and-event-bubbling/artifact.md line 53 verbatim; the payload '' is preventing-cross-site-scripting/artifact.md line 14; the 502 HTML page showing 'Check your internet connection' is handling-http-errors-and-problemdetail-responses/artifact.md lines 42-50. import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL plays no part in any option, so the environment-settings prerequisite is not retrieved. module.json requires 'new scenarios'. Required fix: change the surface of Activities 1 and 3 so they are not the prerequisite pages' own examples, and add at least one interaction between taught topics that no single page showed (for Activity 3, ideally one that makes the API address/environment setting matter); use only taught concepts.

Verified lines 431-434: options A, B and D repeat the same ~20-word construction prefix ('Build each item with createElement, using setAttribute for data-id and textContent for the review text'), so the learner must diff long prose to find the one varying part. Cognitive load is in the education critic's remit (workflow 2.3). Required fix: make the varying part of each option scannable (e.g. state the shared part once or present options as parallel short code), while every option remains self-contained for screen readers and the static alternative. Low severity; may be combined with the edu-p2-06 rewrite.

Verified the artifact.md pattern (hints and sources under '## Cheat sheet', 'Another hint Another hint, 2 of 2 ...', hint-1 summaries dropped, no Sources heading, fit/task/success blocks missing). The cause is the shared generator authoring/tools/qa/md-from-html.mjs, whose line 39 maps '[data-pep-cheat-sheet], [data-section-skip]' to 'Cheat sheet'. artifact.md is 'derived deterministically from artifact.html' (contract), so the page author cannot hand-fix it, and a generator change is repository tooling outside this module branch's scope (authoring/AGENTS.md Delivery). Owner: repository tooling owner, on a separate tooling branch; this branch then only regenerates artifact.md. Not a blocker for this page's correction loop.

Verified the scenario (line 551-552) calls the API through import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL without stating the origin setup, and the course teaches both a same-origin Vite proxy/reverse proxy and real cross-origin traffic with Spring Security CORS (fixing-cors-spring-security-config-vs-vite-dev-proxy/artifact.md lines 17, 48, 70-72). Per the Fetch standard's CORS check, a cross-origin gateway 502 without Access-Control-Allow-Origin becomes a network error and fetch rejects, so option C would still show the connection message; the keyed answer is correct only under an unstated same-origin or CORS-on-errors assumption, and the recap's 'fetch rejects only when no response arrives' (line 650) is false for CORS-blocked responses. Required fix: state the setup in the scenario so the keyed option is correct (same-origin via proxy, or the gateway sends CORS headers), and qualify the recap, the option C explanation, the cheat-sheet comment (line 663) and the static alternative so they do not claim fetch rejects only without a response. Note for the course owner: the prerequisite handling-http-errors page states the same unqualified rule; that is a separate fetch-and-browser-client module follow-up, not this branch.

Verified recap line 647 ('Insert untrusted data as text with textContent or setAttribute') and option A explanation line 431 ('textContent and setAttribute keep visitor text inert') present setAttribute as generally safe. The prerequisite preventing-cross-site-scripting page itself qualifies it ('setAttribute on safe attributes', 'Event handler attributes would be a different story'), and MDN setAttribute Security considerations lists it as an injection sink for handler/URL attributes. Required fix: qualify setAttribute in the recap and option A explanation to plain data/text attributes (not on* handlers or URL/HTML-source attributes); data-id remains a safe use.

Verified option C explanation (line 619) ends 'only a rejected fetch reaches catch'. In the full saveReview code catch also receives a rejected res.json() on a 2xx non-JSON body and any exception from addReview or showMessage; the statement is true only of the !res.ok paths. Required fix: scope the sentence to the error branches (e.g. the connection message is left for a fetch that rejects), in the HTML and the static alternative.

Verified: options A, C and D used the shorthand "Built safely", which was defined only in HTML task step 2, so the Activity 1 static alternative and the artifact.md companion that carries it had an undefined term. The contract requires each interaction to provide an author-written static alternative the Markdown carries, and the companion must be self-contained. Required: define the term inside the static alternative. Checked fix bytes acd5d35e...: data-static-alt (line 432) now begins "Built safely in an option means: each item is created with createElement, its data-id is set with setAttribute and the review text with textContent." The regenerated artifact.md line 148 carries the same definition.

Verified: after the sme-p2-01 fix the scenario sets the request behind the Vite dev proxy (line 555), but report 2 still described a gateway HTML 502. The SME evidence (Vite proxy middleware error handler) shows the dev proxy answers 502 text/plain with an empty body, so the scenario detail was inaccurate for the stated setup (the key was unaffected). Required: the outage description and every explanation that names the 502 body must match the stated setup. Checked fix bytes acd5d35e...: report 2 (line 573) now says the Vite proxy cannot reach Spring Boot and answers 502 with an empty plain-text body. Hint 1 (line 588) asks what res.json() does with a body that is not JSON. The B explanation (line 613) and the C explanation (line 623) and their static-alt text refer to the empty/plain-text 502 with no HTML claim, and artifact.md line 77 matches. The key still holds: res.json() on an empty body rejects with SyntaxError, so the original code and option B still reach catch, while C takes the non-problem else branch.
